claims.text: The solutionized HfNbTaTiZr-based alloy has a homogeneous single-phase microstructure.
Aging the solutionized alloy at 600–800 °C for a few minutes to one hour can produce finely dispersed nanoscale intergranular precipitates.
The targeted intergranular precipitates are ductile.
The targeted precipitates may be tungsten-rich BCC phases.
The intergranular precipitates facilitate localized plasticity.
The intergranular precipitates promote grain-boundary sliding.
The intergranular precipitates retard crack initiation.
Localized plasticity and delayed crack initiation increase alloy ductility.
The aging treatment produces more uniform deformability than solutionizing alone.
The largely unaltered refractory matrix retains high strength after aging.
The largely unaltered refractory matrix retains impact-induced energy-release characteristics after aging.
Tailored aging causes only a minimal reduction, if any, in strength relative to the solutionized baseline.
Tailored aging causes only a minimal reduction, if any, in impact-induced energy release relative to the solutionized baseline.
Over-aging or inadequate process control can cause embrittlement or significant strength loss.

contradictions.description: The stated starting alloy is HfNbTaTiZr-based and no tungsten addition is specified, yet tungsten-rich BCC precipitates are offered as the principal example of phases generated solely by aging. Aging cannot create a tungsten-rich phase unless tungsten is already present but unstated.
